arguments.value:
Parties: Cargill, Incorporated, through its Bio Technology Development Center, and BioAmber S.A.S. The source describes a First Amendment effective July 5, 2011, and later amendments dated October 15, 2011, and October 19, 2011; it does not state a separate overall term or duration for the agreement, only the specific amendment periods and obligations. Governing law: the source does not state any governing law.

This summary covers amendments to a development agreement and a commercial license between Cargill and BioAmber. It allows Cargill, for a limited period in 2011, to add extra work staff under the same compensation terms as the original agreement. It also lets BioAmber fund a research project at the Biotechnology Research Institute, but only until the re-engineered organism proves it can produce succinic acid at a required level, after which BioAmber must stop funding that project and redirect any unused funds elsewhere. In addition, BioAmber may carry out scale-up and production work using the MCC-17 biocatalyst, but it must convert the relevant facilities to use CB1 as the only biocatalyst for succinic acid production and arrange the necessary facility agreements. The commercial license is also amended to require BioAmber to use best efforts to obtain regulatory approvals for CB1 in countries where other strains are used and to scale up CB1 and its fermentation protocols. These amendments do not reduce BioAmber’s existing obligation to replace MCC-17 and its current E. coli strain with CB1 at its existing and future succinic acid production facilities.
